2608.26896.title: AI agents in Algorithmic Electricity Markets: On the Emergence of Tacit Collusion
2608.26896.paper_summary: As electricity market participants increasingly adopt learning-based agents for their bidding strategies, electricity markets are becoming algorithmic. Evidence from algorithmic markets in other domains shows that tacit collusion can arise purely through independent learning. Moreover, electricity markets are typically oligopolistic and feature repeated interaction among a small number of participants, making them structurally susceptible to non-competitive behavior. In the face of these observations, this paper investigates the hypothesis that tacit collusion may emerge in electricity markets where participants' actions are controlled by autonomous learning-based algorithms. We model strategic bidding as a repeated game with imperfect public monitoring, and model the participants' emergent behavior using multi-agent reinforcement learning. We propose a multi-dimensional set of criteria (going beyond profit comparisons against Nash equilibria) to assess whether the resulting behavior constitutes tacit collusion. Our experimental results showcase that such a danger is realistic for electricity markets: there are cases where agents do learn to sustain supra-competitive outcomes that are supportive of tacit collusion indicators, even though the agents were never instructed to collude.
2608.26896.paper_summary_zh: 隨著電力市場參與者越來越多地採用基於學習的代理人來制定其競標策略，電力市場正變得算法化。來自其他領域算法市場的證據顯示，默契共謀可以僅通過獨立學習而產生。此外，電力市場通常是寡頭壟斷的，並且參與者之間存在重複互動，使其在結構上容易受到非競爭行為的影響。面對這些觀察，本文探討了這一假設：在參與者的行為由自主學習算法控制的電力市場中，默契共謀可能會出現。我們將策略性競標建模為一種具有不完美公共監測的重複博弈，並使用多代理強化學習來建模參與者的突現行為。我們提出了一組多維標準（超越與納什均衡的利潤比較）來評估所產生的行為是否構成默契共謀。我們的實驗結果展示了這種風險在電力市場中是現實的：存在一些情況，代理人確實學會了維持支持默契共謀指標的超競爭結果，即使這些代理人從未被指示進行共謀。
2608.26896.author: Jakub Seredyński et.al.
